- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 3x recent mean), model often overcorrects; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 15–30% for 2–4 days post-spike.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias — if forecast is >2.5σ above recent 10-day mean, reduce by 15–25% for next 5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates true volatility; add 10–15% buffer if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” values, model tends to be overly conservative; increase forecast by 5–10% for next 3–7 days.
